items.q: Why does Tan rehabilitate the 'GPT wrapper' slur?
items.a: Out-of-the-box model capability is **not what an enterprise buyer will pay for**. Two gaps: **base-model-to-buyer** (routing, tacit knowledge) and **demo-vs-production** (**95% right, 5% something else** vs click-this-button SaaS).

items.q: What GTM motion does that imply?
items.a: **Forward-deploy AI**: send people **on site** to wire integrations, inject context, and set guardrails. A demo can no longer stand in for proof — you must see it **in production**.

items.q: Why do vertical applied-AI products win?
items.a: They encode one industry's **rules, compliance, and culture**. Prepared (911) is the example: founder knows every buyer, outcome is **faster help**, historically weak software buyers still understand it.

items.q: What must you name before a pilot ends?
items.a: **Identifiable ROI** plus a real sponsor. Coding and support have obvious numbers (output, resolution, CSAT, 24/7, cost). **Partial-flow or augmentation** products struggle to prove the number.

Two axes: **technical completeness** × **liability / culture / regulation**. Lawyer still signs; doctor still owns. Even support keeps **escalation and agent managers**. Excellent tech still fails if no one buys it.
